units.note: All lengths are integer millimetres. All areas are square metres to one decimal. No imperial units appear in this file; imperial-native sources are converted once, at ingest, and the original value is recorded in the source note.

flag_semantics.comment: These six booleans are consumed by the acceptance validator (ticket 07) and the brief defaulting rules (ticket 10). They are DEFINITIONS, not measurements — no reference work supplies them as such. Getting them wrong silently breaks predicates, so each is defined operationally here.
flag_semantics.is_habitable: A room intended for sustained occupation: sleeping, living, dining, working. Drives the window requirement and the exterior-wall requirement (C6 item 4). NOT the same as any national legal definition of 'habitable room' — see the findings doc, section on the kitchen disagreement.
flag_semantics.is_wet: A room containing a plumbed fixture (WC, basin, bath, shower, sink, washing machine). Drives wet-room clustering (C6 item 5).
flag_semantics.is_private: A room that must not lie on the circulation path to any other room. Drives the reachability predicate (C6 item 1): the entry-to-room graph may not route through a room where is_private is true. CORROBORATED, NOT SOURCED, FOR BEDROOMS: AzDTN 2.7-2 cl. 5.9 makes this statutory in AZ -- «Mənzillərdə yataq otaqları digər otağa keçid kimi layihələndirilməməlidir» (bedrooms shall not be designed as a passage to another room), register -məlidir = məcburi. The flag stays region-invariant and engine-defined per C14; this records only that one shipping region independently makes it law. A profile may never move it, because a profile can never change which Plans are rejected. Recorded by ticket 31, which found the clause while harvesting room names.
flag_semantics.needs_window: The room must have at least one window on an exterior wall. Set true wherever is_habitable is true. This is an ENGINE DECISION, not a universal rule — England's Building Regulations impose no daylight requirement at all (see findings). We impose one because a Homeowner judges by 'would I live here'.
flag_semantics.counts_as_otaq: Whether a Room of this type contributes 1 to the otaq count -- the unit C13's PRODUCT PROMISE is stated in, and the number a Baku listing prints. NOT is_habitable, and the two are deliberately separate fields: is_habitable drives the window and exterior-wall requirement (C6 item 4), counts_as_otaq drives what the copy claims. They agree on seventeen of eighteen types and disagree on `kitchen_dining`. Sourced where AzDTN 2.7-2 cl. 5.5 enumerates yaşayış otaqları and cl. 5.2 enumerates yardımçı sahələr; derived only where a type falls under cl. 5.5's unqualified `otaq`. See [[Otaq]] in CONTEXT.md, and ADR 0013, which asked for a flag named `habitable` -- renamed here because a field called `habitable` sitting beside `is_habitable` and meaning something else is a defect, not a schema.
flag_semantics.brief_nameable: Whether a Homeowner may name this room type in a Brief. False only for types `resolve` invents. Requested by docs/spec/brief.md section 3, which gives the Brief the ergonomic key set verbatim and names this flag as the exception mechanism; the JSON Schema generator (brief.md section 10) reads it.
flag_semantics.is_habitable_versus_counts_as_otaq: READ THIS BEFORE USING EITHER. `is_habitable` is a GEOMETRY driver: it decides whether a Space needs a window and an exterior wall. `counts_as_otaq` is a PRODUCT driver: it decides what number the copy prints and what C13's 1-4 band is measured in. `kitchen_dining` is habitable and is not an otaq. Neither field may be computed from the other.

region_model.comment: Rewritten by ticket 14, *Which region profiles ship in v1*. See ADR 0006. The corpus split argument from ticket 5 stands: body-derived clearances are region-invariant, convention-derived numbers are not. What changed is which regions exist and what a profile is FOR. After ticket 7 moved every hard dimensional floor to the region-invariant ergonomic layer, a region profile governs printed and built conventions only -- it can change which Plans are PREFERRED and which strings are PRINTED, never which Plans are REJECTED. The single exception is model.thickness_in_catalogue, which is hard.
region_model.shipping_region_rationale: A profile is a construction system plus a drawing convention; country is only a proxy for it, and a poor one. UK's stud-and-cavity build-up exists in neither corpus nor deployment context. The SNiP-family residential norm AzDTN derives from is written for multi-apartment buildings, which is the only building type any corpus on this map contains. Its brick (120/250/380/510) and panel (80/140/160) series are expected to satisfy even_thickness_required where DIN 4172's octametric series (115/365/490) systematically does not. Its sources are freely published, which keeps the copyright posture of findings section 7.6 intact. And it is the place a plan would actually be built.
region_model.test_fixture_rationale: Never selectable by a user. Every UK number here was read first-hand from a Crown-copyright document under the Open Government Licence v3.0 -- the only profile that is free, complete, independently checkable end to end, and lawfully redistributable. The test suite asserts the profile MECHANISM against it: schema, tier resolution, the even-thickness rule, decimal separator, abbreviation fallback. Ticket 5 called this 'a testing decision, not a claim that UK numbers are better'; ticket 14 took it at its word and split the shipping role from the verification role.

regions_deleted.DE: Three independent disqualifications, any one sufficient. Its canonical internal partition is 115 mm and the whole octametric series 115/365/490 is odd, which ADR 0004 forbids. Every DE number here is REPORTED from documents the research records as not read. Building the profile would mean transcribing Neufert's tables into a data file, which findings section 7.6 item 7 names as the specific infringement this project would walk into by accident. It survived only as a default_region label that was itself a proxy for Swiss data.
regions_deleted.US: Never populated, no consumer, and light frame widens the divergence rather than narrowing it.
regions_deleted.IN, JP, AU, CN: Stubs with no sources and no consumer. Removed rather than carried.

region_model.corpus_provenance_is_a_separate_field: RegionProfile and CorpusProvenance are two fields with two enums. In v1 they hold AZ and CH and their disagreement is the normal case, not a defect. Retrieval reads Swiss Dwellings only, so the engine draws Swiss-shaped layouts to Azerbaijani conventions, permanently. That is a disclosed product limit, not a bug. At inference the model is conditioned on the CH/swiss tokens it was trained with; an AZ token that never appeared in training is undefined behaviour, not localisation.
region_model.must_match_STRUCK: Previously: 'The region enum here MUST be the same enum as the training-data conditioning variable in ticket 06.' Struck by ticket 14. Read literally it forbids a UK profile forever, because that enum's members are fixed by corpora we hold. Its justification -- that projecting a region-A proposal onto region-B constraints is strictly worse than either alone -- predates ticket 7 removing every hard dimensional floor from the region layer. Replaced by profile_carried_for_life.
region_model.profile_carried_for_life: A Plan carries its region profile id from Brief to export. The solver and the validator MUST read the same one: model.thickness_in_catalogue is hard, so a Plan solved under one thickness catalogue fails validation under another.
region_model.even_thickness_required: Every wall thickness in every profile MUST be an even number of millimetres. ADR 0001 needs erode(rect, t_int/2) in integer millimetres and ADR 0004's tier-1 overall needs t_party/2. 100/120/140/200/240/300 pass; 115 and 125 do not. See ADR 0004.
region_model.thickness_catalogue_is_engine_choice: Measured, not assumed -- experiments/corpus-smoke/wall_thickness_swiss.py over 199,210 Swiss Dwellings WALL separators. The corpus has NO module: 59.1% of walls fall within +/-2 mm of a multiple of 10 against 50% for uniform noise, the modal snapped value (80 mm) holds 5.60%, and the distribution is near-continuous from 50 to 600 mm (p25 109, p50 169, p75 267). An 8-entry catalogue covers 58.5% of real walls at +/-10 mm. So the catalogue cannot be derived from the corpus and must be an ENGINE_CHOICE bounded by that range. Corpus thickness never reaches a produced Plan in any case: retrieval supplies arrangement, and ADR 0001 re-derives geometry from our own t_int.

tier_model.comment: A single number per cell is not recoverable from the sources; England alone yields five different 'minimum bedroom areas' depending on which instrument you invoke. Tier disambiguates.

tiers.statutory_floor: The hardest number any instrument in that region imposes. Below this a plan is rejected. Deliberately permissive — it is a floor, not a goal.
tiers.market_default: What is actually built and what a Homeowner expects. This is what unstated brief fields default to (ticket 10) and what the solver targets.
tiers.accessible: The region's wheelchair-user tier. Not a v1 default; carried so that adopting it later is a parameter change, not a rewrite.

tier_model.default_tier_rationale: C2 says the Homeowner judges by 'would I live here'. A plan built to the statutory floor is legal and unliveable. Defaulting to the floor would make the engine reliably produce plans nobody wants.

validator_binding.hard_reject_below_note: Was null, then 'statutory_floor'. Ticket 7 found that binding unusable and named the ergonomic minimum instead; ticket 19 authored the layer and this now names it by the key it actually has. Region-invariant because bodies are. data/acceptance/rules.json tier_binding must hold the same string; a conformance test asserts it.
validator_binding.statutory_floor_note: Ticket 14: a warn, never a gate, and only where non-null. AZ is the first region where it is non-null at all -- SNiP-family norms prescribe minimum room areas where German law prescribes none. CRITICAL: the disclosure wording derives from the cited source's `force` field, not from the tier's name. Printing 'below statutory minimum' for a plan that breaks no law is exactly the legal claim C8 forbids; under the UK NDSS (force: planning_policy_optional) it would be wrong more often than right.

ru_vsn_62_91.force_note: AZERBAIJAN'S ACCESSIBILITY INSTRUMENT, not SNiP 35-01-2001 and not SP 59.13330 — those are Russian and return ZERO hits across all 211 pages of the Azerbaijani SİYAHI. ru_vsn_62_91.scope_warning: cl. 5.1.3 sets communal room areas for дома-интернаты (residential institutions serving a whole living group), NOT rooms in a dwelling. Do not mine it into the wet-room row — a 12 m2 'bathroom' is a shared institutional facility.

The ticket budgeted for REPORTED values off SNiP/SP ancestors and that fallback proved unnecessary: arxkom.gov.az serves the normative PDFs on an unauthenticated GET. construction.comment: ONE construction type and ONE t_int, and the arithmetic forced it rather than taste choosing it. Over 19 sourced candidate thicknesses the set of pairs sharing a residue class mod 250 is EMPTY, and structurally so: the fired-brick series steps by 130 and the RC-panel series by 20, neither of which 250 divides. Under ADR 0007 a second t_int would need a second copy of every linear minimum. See ship_gates.adr_0007_single_t_int_decision. ADR 0010 makes every thickness here a LAYER SET: the unsuffixed key is the total and is the only one anything consumes.
construction.shipping_type_rationale: The only type with an AZ-verified value for every field, even by construction, and the commonest multi-apartment wall system in Azerbaijan -- which is the only building type any corpus on this map holds.

t_finish.note: Cement-sand plaster over stone or brick masonry. Read first-hand from Elave 8* Cedvel 1, column 'Layin qalinligi, mm'; row 28 gives the same 15 mm for lime mortar. WAS engine_choice, and no longer is -- docs/research/az-finish-layer.md. pdftotext scrambled that table, so the column assignment was verified from GLYPH COORDINATES (experiments/finish-layer/verify_appendix8_columns.py): the 15 sits at x=341 inside the thickness column (neighbours 1,5 / 3-4 / 100 / 250-400 at x=325-349), not the resistance column at x=470-495. SCOPE, AND IT MATTERS: App. 8* is a CHARACTERISTICS table -- it states an air-permeation resistance AT a stated layer thickness. The norm TABULATES 15 mm; it does not REQUIRE it, and no code-compliance claim is made (C8). THE TRAP THAT WAS AVOIDED: the retained finishing-works norm SNiP 3.04.01-87 does grade plaster simple/improved/high-quality, but Table 9's classes are FLATNESS TOLERANCES of 1-3 mm/m, NOT thicknesses; reading that ladder as thickness would have shipped t_finish = 1/2/3 mm and been internally consistent all the way down, with no arithmetic gate catching it. Table 10 bounds thickness (single-layer <= 20 non-gypsum) rather than specifying it. COMPETING NUMBER: AzDTN 2.17-1 cl. 8.24 note 1 implies 10 mm per face, exact over three panel sizes -- but for FACTORY BRICK PANELS (type B1), cast against a flat pallet, not hand-laid masonry, which must absorb bricklaying deviation. Recorded against B1 if B1 ever ships. See az-finish-layer.md section 4.

t_int.note: TOTAL. Was 120 (bare half-brick), which put the Space boundary on the STRUCTURAL face while four documents claimed finished faces -- and put a 1700 mm bath inside a 1670 mm bathroom minimum. ADR 0010. MOVES THE ADR 0007 RESIDUE CLASS FROM 130 TO 100 mod 250.

t_int_structural.note: Half-brick bare masonry. Corroborated by gost_530_2012 Table 3 working width with cl. 3.12. Consumed by nothing in v1; carried for IFC layers and for the deferred structural patch.

t_ext_total.note: PROVISIONAL. 380 leaf + 100 insulation + 20 finish. az_azdtn_2_12_4 Table 4 asks R >= 2.1 and a 380 brick leaf gives about 0.7, so a build-up is required -- but Baku's degree-day figure Dd could not be obtained, so the total is not yet derivable. Flagged, not hidden. ADR 0010: this number was ALREADY a total including its 20 mm inner finish, so it is unchanged -- the external wall was finished-face all along and only t_int disagreed. Ticket 35: its 20 mm finish share is NOT supported by AzDTN 2.12-4* App. 8* -- the only 20 mm row there is lime-gypsum plaster over TIMBER, and the document's external-render reference gives colours, not thicknesses. Still engine_choice, still blocked on Baku's Dd, and now known to be unsupported on a second axis.

t_party.note: TOTAL. 250 one-brick leaf + 15 our finish + 15 the neighbour's. Drawn thickness. NOT eroded: a party wall sits on the Envelope, whose inner face is given, so only partitions are eroded. ADR 0010 deletes ADR 0004's tier-1 centreline exception, so t_party/2 now has no consumer at all.

t_party_structural.note: One brick. No code publishes a party-wall THICKNESS; it is derived from the acoustic and fire requirements. The acoustic rows are 'brick + 15 plaster both sides': 250 computes to 52 dB and passes, 120 to 49 dB and FAILS. Note the AZ/RU divergence: Azerbaijan requires 50 dB, not Russia's 52. THIS ROW IS WHY t_finish IS 15.

residue_class_mod_grid.note: ADR 0007, restated at ADR 0010's t_int. mapping.comment:
THE MAPPING IS THE VOCABULARY; THE TABLES ABOVE ARE JUST VALUES. Every vocabulary question this file had is answered here and nowhere else, so `areas_m2` and `clear_widths_mm` stay exactly as their sources key them -- `areas_m2` is a faithful transcription of cl. 5.7's bullet list and renaming its cells would break the only thing they are for, which is provenance. The defect ticket 31 opened was never the names. It was that no object stated the bridge between them.

TOTAL BY CONSTRUCTION: one row for every one of the eighteen ergonomic keys, and a conformance test asserts that. A row is never absent; an unmapped cell is an explicit null.
mapping.direction: Ergonomic is canonical and the Brief speaks it verbatim (brief.md section 3). This maps ergonomic -> AZ and is never read the other way. It is the same shape as proposer.md section 4.1's retrieval-class projection: lossy, one-way, and declared.
mapping.null_means: NO SOFT TARGET, NOT AN ERROR. `dim.market_default_area` skips a Space whose az_area resolves to null; it does not raise and it does not fall back. This is C14 read literally -- a profile may change which Plans are PREFERRED, never which are REJECTED, so a profile with no preference for a room type is a legal profile and silence is the normal case. Ten of eighteen keys are silent in AZ. The hard floor always resolves, because it is ergonomic and region-invariant.
mapping.conditioning:
ONE AXIS, NAMED, AND NO EXPRESSION LANGUAGE: `when_otaq_count`. Three AZ area cells condition on the same thing -- cl. 5.7's `birotaqlı mənzil` -- and nothing in the profile conditions on anything else: living_room_1room_flat vs living_room_2plus, kitchen_niche, and wardrobe_1room_entry. `when_otaq_count: 1` matches a one-otaq dwelling; `null` is the unguarded fallthrough and MUST be last. First match wins.

WHY HERE AND NOT IN THE KEY OR THE PARSER. Encoding it in the key is what produced the defect -- `living_room_1room_flat` is not a room type, it is a room type conditioned on the dwelling. Resolving it at Brief-parse time buries a profile fact in the parser, so a second profile with a different axis becomes a code change; C14 says a profile is data. The mapping is already profile-scoped and already about translation, so the condition belongs to it.

A SECOND AXIS IS KNOWN TO EXIST AND IS NOT LIVE. *Dimensional standards corpus* found AD M's LKD area stated as 25 + 2 x (bedspaces - 2) -- conditioned on bedspaces, not otaq. UK ships no areas and is never selectable (C12), so v1 needs one axis. Adding the second is a SCHEMA change, not a data change, and this note exists so that is discovered before it is designed around.

WHAT THE GUARD ACTUALLY BUYS IN V1, MEASURED: almost nothing on the default tier, and this is recorded so nobody reads it as load-bearing. living_room_1room_flat and living_room_2plus have DIFFERENT statutory floors (15,0 / 16,0) and the SAME market_default (16,0), and market_default is the default tier and the solver's target -- so for `living` the guard changes only the statutory WARN, never the soft target. The other two conditioned cells, kitchen_niche and wardrobe_1room_entry, are unreachable in v1. The axis is real, sourced and correctly placed; it simply does not pay out yet. It is built now because encoding it in the key is what broke this file once, and because the cost of the guard is one field.

conformance.resolvable_means: THE LOOKUP IS TOTAL, NOT THAT A NUMBER COMES BACK. Ticket 31's closing check reads 'for every room type the Brief can name, both a hard floor and a soft target are resolvable'. Ten keys have no AZ area, and the stricter reading could only be satisfied by inventing ten Azerbaijani numbers -- the exact C8 failure. So: every hard floor is non-null (it is ergonomic, and always resolves), and every soft target resolves to a cell or to an explicit null per mapping.null_means.

area_ratio.note: 1:8, a LOWER bound, applying to living rooms and kitchens. The light opening counts windows plus the open aperture of a loggia.

area_ratio_upper_bound.note: EXPLICITLY NULL. AZ states no cap. The 1:5.5 figure the ticket quoted is a MAXIMUM-glazing cap, usually quoted backwards, and it belongs to su_snip_2_08_01_89 -- repealed for AZ on 2021-11-30 -- and to ru_sp_54_13330, which has no force here.

area_ratio_soft_target.note: About 1:6.5, the solver's soft objective. NOT an AZ rule. Chosen because 1:6.5 is itself a published cap in SNiP II-L.1-71* rather than an invented average. 0.125 remains the only AZ floor.

The norm neither requires nor excuses daylight for it. head_datum_mm.ref: the balcony door's own catalogue head; see docs/research/vertical-dimensions.md
head_datum_mm.note: ONE CONSTANT, AND EVERY WINDOW SILL IS DERIVED FROM IT -- ADR 0012. AzDTN 2.7-2 publishes NO window sill height ('pəncərə altlığı': ZERO occurrences in the full 2021 text), so a sill cannot be quoted, and a per-room-type table would be four invented numbers. Instead ONE datum, and it is NOT invented: 2200 is the balcony door's own catalogue head (BS 22-7,5), taken because A BALCONY DOOR AND THE WINDOW BESIDE IT SHARE A LINTEL -- the ordinary post-Soviet living-room composition -- so the tallest catalogue opening sets the head line and every window hangs from it. sill = head_datum - catalogue H. Structure derived, one constant chosen from the catalogue rather than from nowhere: ADR 0009's shape. Doors sit 100 mm below the line at their own 2100, which is what a real elevation does. Gated: head_datum <= h_clear, and every window H <= head_datum.

openings.sill_rule: DERIVED, NEVER STORED PER INSTANCE. sill = openings.head_datum_mm - catalogue H. On the shipped catalogue: window_living (OR 15-15, H 1500) = 700; window_bedroom (OR 15-12, H 1500 -- the mark is HEIGHT-width, so 1500 x 1200) = 700; window_kitchen (OS 12-9, H 1200) = 1000, which clears a 900 mm kitchen counter and is why the kitchen window is the short one. All even, so ADR 0004 holds on derived sills as well as on openings. Fills annotation.md's window-schedule 'Sill height' column. A sill is NOT a catalogue column: the same OR 15-15 sits at one height in a living room and another over a counter, so the catalogue fixes H x W and the datum fixes placement.

fall_barrier_mm.note: STATUTORY. Verbatim cl. 8.3: «Pilləkən, balkon, lociya, terras, dam və yıxılma təhlükəsi olan digər yerlərdə məhəccərlərin hündürlüyü 1,2 m-dən az olmamalıdır.» Register 'az olmamalıdır' = məcburi. Corroborated at cl. 8.10 (1,2 m məhəccər on trafficable flat roofs). WINDOWS ARE NOT NAMED: the clause reaches them only through «yıxılma təhlükəsi olan digər yerlər» -- other places where there is a risk of falling -- so the HEIGHT is verified and the TRIGGER is not. Fills annotation.md's window-schedule 'Fall barrier' column and finally supplies CONTEXT.md's Fall barrier term, which until now was defined with nothing behind it.

openings.fall_barrier_when_required: REFUSED, NOT CHOSEN, AND THE REASON IS THE MODEL'S SCOPE. cl. 8.3 fixes the guarding HEIGHT and reaches windows only through «yıxılma təhlükəsi olan digər yerlər» -- other places where there is a RISK OF FALLING. Whether a window is such a place depends on the DROP BELOW IT, which depends on which storey the dwelling sits on and what is outside. v1 has exactly one Storey at Elevation 0.0, IfcSite is out of scope, and the map rules out the site entirely -- so this engine cannot evaluate the trigger AT ALL. A ground-floor window needs no barrier; the same window on the eighth floor does; nothing in the model distinguishes them. So v1 publishes the height and refuses the trigger: annotation.md's 'Fall barrier' column reads '—' for every window, which that spec already provides for ('where the model holds one, and — where it does not'). Picking a sill threshold here would have been a SAFETY claim with no source and no way to evaluate it -- the exact C8 breach ticket 25 exists to prevent. This is a refusal in the same class as accessibility and as the ergonomic layer's height.

drawing.language_costs_nothing_in_abbreviations: The feared trade -- that choosing Azerbaijani forces us to invent an abbreviation set, which findings 7.6 forbids -- IS NOT ARMED, because NO published room-name abbreviation set exists in ANY of the three candidate languages. gost_2316_2008 cl. 4.4 actively FORBIDS abbreviating outside a list containing zero room words.

thousands_separator.note: NONE. CLDR gives '.' as the az group separator, so a grouped 4.400 would be misread as a decimal. Never group.

room_names_az.comment: The drafting standards fix the naming RULE, not the vocabulary. These terms are AzDTN 2.7-2's own, cross-read from the minima and daylight partials -- which closes the gap the drawing partial could not. The technical term for a room-as-space is yerleshke, not otaq.
room_names_az.ascii_note: Values here are ASCII-folded for JSON hygiene in this file. The DRAWING must emit the correct Azerbaijani orthography -- schwa, gh, dotless i, oe, sh, ue, ch -- which is why the DXF version floor has to rise. See dxf_encoding_floor. The canonical spellings are in the findings doc.

dxf_encoding_floor.note: MEASURED, not assumed. The Azerbaijani alphabet is UNREPRESENTABLE in DXF R2000: no legacy code page anywhere encodes the schwa character, not even Turkish cp1254, which carries every other Azerbaijani letter. R2007+ is clean. Russian is WORSE at R2000, not better -- cp1251 cannot encode the superscript two used by m2. This CONTRADICTS docs/research/bim-cad-export-stack.md, whose line that 'R2000+ is unicode-capable' is false in general. Nothing shipped is broken: annotation cl. 11 already writes R2010. The STATED FLOOR must rise.

drawing.sheet_mark_conflict: UNRESOLVED, and handed on. azs_21101_2010 Elave A marks architectural working drawings MH (Memarliq helli) or MT, where annotation cl. 9/10 numbers sheets A-101 on the US NCS convention and cl. 11 layers them A-WALL on AIA. A drawing issued in Azerbaijani to an Azerbaijani builder with a US sheet number is internally inconsistent. Layer names are a machine-facing interchange convention and have their own justification; the SHEET NUMBER, which the builder reads, is the one worth reconsidering.

instrument.note: Chosen over az_housing_code art. 12.5. Both are in force and both define umumi sahe; they disagree only on balconies, which v1 cannot express. The Qaydalar is the DESIGN AND INVENTORY instrument -- which is what a drawing is, what a technical passport is, and therefore what an Azerbaijani property listing quotes -- and cl. 3.2, the measurement rule adopted below, lives inside it. The Housing Code is a housing-law ENTITLEMENT test and was never a drawing convention.

measurement_plane.v: finished inner face of walls and partitions, at floor level, skirtings excluded
measurement_plane.note: THE CLAUSE THAT BOUND V1, now obeyed. ADR 0001 eroded t_int/2 from a centreline where t_int was the BARE leaf, yielding the structural face and overstating every area. ADR 0010 makes t_int a total, so the erosion lands on the finished face by construction and no second plane exists.

quantity.note: umumi sahe SUMS ROOM AREAS, so internal partitions are NOT counted. This is NOT GIA, which counts them. On a 90 m2 dwelling the partition footprint is 5.7 percent of Sum(Space area) at the shipped t_int of 150 -- WIDER than the acceptance bar's own 5 percent total-area gate (ticket 33, measured over 14,063 dwellings; the corpus's own partitions are 4.8 percent and our footprint at the old 120 was 4.5, so the 4-5 first written was right for the value ADR 0010 REPLACED and stale for the one it shipped), which is why the gate had to change QUANTITY and not merely tolerance. Hall, corridor, lobby and store are included: umumi sahe counts habitable and ancillary spaces alike.

area_convention.carried: ONE value per Plan, derived from this profile and carried for life alongside the region profile id -- never per Space, which would be twenty copies of one fact. Printed once in the title block AREAS attribute, written once into IFC. The Brief carries its OWN target_area_convention, separately, and the two are allowed to disagree; a disagreement is a hard BRIEF error.
area_convention.brief_semantics: target_area means INTERIOR umumi sahe with balcony, loggia, terrace and eyvan EXCLUDED. A Baku listing quotes umumi sahe INCLUDING them at cl. 3.8 coefficients, and an eyvan enters at 1.0 -- FULL area, not reduced -- so a homeowner's '90 m2' can be several percent more than the rooms they will get. The engine does NOT guess a balcony share back out; it surfaces the reading as an Assumption per C4. Owed by the Brief and the Homeowner surface.

area_convention.housing_code_delta: az_housing_code art. 12.5 EXCLUDES balconies outright where cl. 3.8 includes them at a coefficient. Both statutory, both in force. INERT in v1 -- no balcony, no ceiling height -- so the two compute the same number today. The moment a balcony or a storey height enters the model this becomes load-bearing and the instrument choice above starts to bite.
area_convention.there_is_no_zhilaya_ploshchad: THE FINDING THAT MATTERS. Azerbaijan publishes no living-area metric. The modern instruments did not ADD a total-area figure alongside a living-area one -- they REPLACED the pair. The ticket's framing of the handoff as a PAIR is wrong.

ship_gates.adr_0004_even_thickness: PASS -- every shipped thickness even, TOTALS AND LEAVES ALIKE: 15, 120, 150, 250, 280, 380, 500. ADR 0001 needs erode(rect, t_int/2) in integer millimetres and 150/2 = 75. Asserted by experiments/region-profile/gate_check.py -- RE-RUN OWED at the new t_int.
ship_gates.adr_0004_even_opening: PASS -- every shipped OPENING dimension even. Block sizes excluded and never keyed off.
ship_gates.adr_0007_single_t_int_decision: DECIDED HERE, and the arithmetic forced it. The ticket offered three shapes -- a single internal thickness, per-thickness minima, or forcing the grid question open. Taken: A SINGLE t_int, now 150 mm total (ADR 0010). Per-thickness minima was rejected because it needs N copies of every dimensional minimum AND a Plan carrying its construction type for life, extending profile_carried_for_life, for a fidelity gain v1 cannot show a Homeowner. The grid question is left open where ADR 0007 left it. SUPERSEDED IN ITS REASONING, NOT ITS CONCLUSION (ticket 33): 'N copies of every dimensional minimum' is FALSE BY COUNT -- ADR 0009 exempts the ergonomic layer and profiles.AZ publishes ZERO linear minima, so N copies of zero rows is zero rows. The single t_int still holds, on a different argument: the cost that binds is ADR 0001 consequence 5 and the HARD validator rule model.space_matches_erosion, neither of which ADR 0009 touches. docs/research/single-internal-thickness.md s4.
ship_gates.adr_0007_scope_carve_out: STILL OWED, and narrower than ADR 0009. ADR 0009 exempts the ergonomic LAYER; ADR 0007 still binds region profiles, and as written it binds 'every dimensional minimum published in a region profile'. Only a linear minimum the solver posts on a room's CLEAR rect is eroded by t_int. AREAS in m2, STOREY HEIGHTS, DOOR CLEAR WIDTHS and WHEELCHAIR TURNING SQUARES must NOT be aligned. Moot for AZ, which publishes no hard linear minimum at all, but owed before a second profile publishes one.
ship_gates.adr_0007_unresolved_collision: RESOLVED, and not by this ticket. ADR 0007's move is to publish the largest admissible value AT OR BELOW the source's figure, justified by reading that figure as nominal or centreline-to-centreline. That is a UNIT CONVERSION and is available only for a number quoted from a source. A body-derived ergonomic clearance is already clear by definition, so there is nothing to convert -- and az_azdtn_2_7_2 cl. 5.6 puts EVERY intra-apartment linear minimum in that invariant layer, so this is where all of them are. Measured: 36 of the 36 hard linear minima in the `ergonomic` layer miss the residue class. ADR 0009 (*Ergonomic minima and the constraint table's missing half*, accepted 2026-08-21) settles it the same way from the other side: the congruence rule is a REGION-PROFILE SHIP GATE ONLY, the ergonomic layer is exempt, published minima stay millimetre-exact, the solver's ceiling absorbs the remainder, and the v1 grid stays at 250 mm. NOTE that ADR 0009 also refutes the feared cost: ADR 0007's 4-/5-/6-room deletion tracked the minima's MAGNITUDE against the placeholder table, not the congruence, and does not reproduce at the derived floor. The real cost of snapping is the WC, whose whole real width distribution spans under two grid steps: 23.0 percent rejected becomes 56.1 percent.
ship_gates.adr_0010_measurement_plane: DECIDED by ticket 17. The Space boundary is the innermost finish face; t_int is a total. Consequence carried openly: ticket 19's room-count deletion analysis (the 4/5/6-room deletion narrowing to {5, and 6 unknown}) was computed at t_int = 120 and is RE-OWED at 150. Direction not guessed.
ship_gates.ticket_33_sanity_check: PASS, and by a wide margin. The corpus-optimal SINGLE internal thickness over 411 km of Swiss internal wall is 146 mm; this profile ships 150, reached from AzDTN 2.17-1's half-brick and AzDTN 2.12-4*'s plaster with no corpus involved. Misplaced material 38.1 percent at 150 against 38.0 at the optimum. CORRECTS the '150 sits below the corpus median, near the p25' framing: that quoted the ALL-WALLS census, which mixes in exterior and party walls at 2-3x a partition. INTERNAL walls only: p25=100, p50=131, p75=169, so 150 sits at about p60, ABOVE the internal median.

The guarding HEIGHT (cl. 8.3, 1,2 m) is verified; sill and trigger are engine_choice and say so. A measured negative, in the same class as ticket 14's 'the corpus has no module at all'.

ergonomic.comment: The region-invariant hard floor, and the whole hard dimensional reject set of the acceptance bar. Every value is DERIVED -- a sum of published fixture footprints plus the body zone below -- never transcribed from a table. Findings section 7.6 item 12 requires this; it is also the strongest copyright hygiene available, because the row set, the programmes and the arithmetic are ours.

reading.dimensions_are_clear: Every value is a CLEAR dimension, per ADR 0001 -- what an occupant can tape between finished faces. Nothing here is nominal or centreline, so nothing here has t_int to subtract.
reading.short_and_long_not_width_and_depth: A room has no canonical orientation, so the pair is (shorter side, longer side), not (x, y). Findings section 8 set min_width = min_depth for orientation-free rooms and made bathroom and wc directional exceptions; that distinction DISSOLVES under this reading -- the acceptance rules are already stated over the shorter and longer clear dimension, so every room publishes a (short, long) pair and no room needs an axis binding. Most room types turn out non-square once fixtures drive the rectangle, not just the two.
reading.area_is_not_redundant: area is short x long rounded DOWN to 0.1 m2. Rounded up it would reject the very rectangle it was derived from. It binds independently because a room may satisfy both sides and still be long and thin -- dim.aspect_ratio_hard catches that separately.
reading.adr_0007_does_not_apply_here: ADR 0007 requires a published minimum to satisfy min + t_int = 0 (mod grid). That rule is sound for a CONVENTION-derived number, where the source quoted a nominal or centreline figure and subtracting t_int recovers the clear one, and UNSOUND for a derivation-derived one, which is already clear and has nothing to subtract. A derived 1700 mm IS the bath; rounding it down to 1650 deletes 50 mm of bathtub. Measured: snapping this layer onto the 250 mm lattice costs the wc floor about 10 points of real corpus. So the ergonomic layer publishes millimetre-precise minima and the solver's ceiling absorbs the remainder; ADR 0007 continues to bind on the region profile, whose numbers are quoted.

body_zone.note: The single free parameter: the depth of body in front of a fixture that cannot be shared with another fixture's zone. Fitted so that no room type's floor rejects more than about 5% of fixture-consistent real rooms in Swiss Dwellings (experiments/region-profile/floor_calibration.py). It lands on 300 mm, which is also Neufert's stated minimum clearance from a WC pan's free side to a wall -- fitted and cited agree. NOT 750 mm: AD M's 750 is a wheelchair transfer space, and composing a private bathroom out of accessibility figures produces a floor that rejects a third of real homes.

ergonomic.flags_note: The four booleans are DEFINITIONS, stated operationally in flag_semantics, and no reference work supplies them. They are published here per room type because data/acceptance/rules.json consumes them -- circ.no_private_transit, win.habitable_has_window, win.exterior_wall and wet.plumbing_group_count all read one -- and before this they existed only as prose in findings section 8. A flag the registry cannot read is a predicate that silently does not fire, which is the same failure as a missing minimum. ONE CORRECTION to findings section 8: it sets study is_private false, while CONTEXT.md defines the Private room class as 'a Brief's bedroom, study or nursery, as one class' and the Proposer spec collapses {ROOM, BEDROOM, STUDIO} to PRIVATE on the same reasoning. A study that is a thoroughfare to another room is not a study. Set true here; section 8 predates the glossary entry.

corpus_label_split.comment: *What the model proposes* handed this ticket the BATHROOM split, on the reasoning that the threshold is the boundary between two rooms' minima and so falls out of this table. MEASURED, THAT IS WRONG. Two floors are both floors: wc is 0.8 m2 and shower_room 1.4 m2, and a threshold there misclassifies 19% of the corpus. The classes differ in their DISTRIBUTIONS, not their minima -- real WCs sit at a median 1.85 m2 and real bathrooms at 4.17 -- so the splitter has to be fitted, and it is fitted against fixture ground truth rather than invented: Swiss Dwellings carries BATHTUB, SHOWER and TOILET features, so which rooms really are bathrooms is known.
corpus_label_split.label: BATHROOM

threshold_m2.note: Fitted over 66,386 fixture-labelled rooms. Total misclassification 5.9% at 2.4 m2 against a measured optimum of 5.8% at 2.45; 2.4 is published because the curve is flat there and the round number is honest about the precision. The derived candidates the ticket expected -- 3.6 and 4.0 -- score 23.3% and 36.9%. Adding the long side as a second test buys nothing: the best two-term rule collapses back onto the area term.

error_direction.measured: At 2.4 m2, 1.5% of real bathrooms are called wc and 4.4% of real WCs are called bathroom. It prefers to over-assign to `bathroom`, by about three to one.
error_direction.why_that_direction_is_tolerable: An over-large wc wastes floor and breaks nothing. A bathroom that is really a WC arrives with too little room for a bath -- but it is still a real, built Swiss room and still clears the bathroom floor of 1.7 m2, so it produces a small bathroom, not an invalid Plan. Neither error moves a published minimum, because no minimum here is fitted to the corpus.

validated_against_corpus.comment: *Rectangularising real rooms* set the principle: every corpus dwelling is a real, built, QA'd home, so a hard rule that rejects them measures what our model cannot express. A derived floor is therefore not self-justifying and every value above was checked against Swiss Dwellings. The low tail is REAL, not annotation debris: 0% of wc rooms fail to hold a pan, 0.8% of bathroom rooms fail to hold a 1700 mm bath.
validated_against_corpus.weakest_cells_note: Swiss Dwellings carries no label for these, so they are derived and UNFALSIFIED. study is the weakest number in the file: a one-desk programme with no corpus to check it against and no source that states a study minimum.
